cards.text: Israel has seen the wall of Jericho fall (Joshua 6:20). But the Israelites acted unfaithfully regarding the things devoted to destruction. A man named Achan, from the tribe of Judah, took some of what was set apart.

cards.question: One man took the devoted things. Who does the anger of the LORD burn against?

cards.text: Meanwhile, Joshua sends men from Jericho to spy out Ai, a town near Beth-aven, east of Bethel. I bet nobody has told Joshua about Achan.

cards.question: The spies come back from Ai. True or false: they tell Joshua to send all the people up to attack it.

cards.text: They say two or three thousand men are enough, because the people of Ai are so few. That's me looking at one little batch of dough and deciding I don't need a timer for THIS one.

cards.question: So about three thousand Israelites go up to Ai. What happens?

answers.text: They flee before the men of Ai
They capture Ai in one day

cards.text: The men of Ai strike down about thirty-six Israelites. They chase them from the gate as far as the quarries and strike them down on the slopes.

cards.question: True or false: after the loss at Ai, the people of Israel lose heart.

cards.text: Joshua tears his clothes and falls facedown before the ark of the LORD. The elders of Israel do the same, and they all sprinkle dust on their heads.

cards.question: How long does Joshua stay facedown before the ark of the LORD?
Joshua asks the Lord GOD why He ever brought this people across the Jordan, only to hand them to the Amorites. What does Joshua wish they had done?

answers.text: Stayed on the other side of the Jordan
Stayed back in the land of Egypt
Waited longer in the camp at Jericho

cards.text: Then Joshua says, "O Lord, what can I say, now that Israel has turned its back and run from its enemies?" That's a man who doesn't know what to say, and he says it anyway, straight to God.

cards.question: Joshua thinks ahead to when the Canaanites and everyone in the land hear about Ai. What does he say they will do?

answers.text: Surround Israel and wipe out its name

cards.question: True or false: Joshua ends his prayer by asking what God will do for His great name.

cards.text: But the LORD says to Joshua, "Stand up! Why have you fallen on your face?"

cards.question: The LORD tells Joshua why the Israelites could not stand against their enemies at Ai. What is the reason?

answers.text: Israel took what was devoted to destruction
Joshua sent too few men up to Ai
The men of Ai had a mightier army

cards.text: And the LORD doesn't stop there. He says they have transgressed His covenant, stolen and lied, and put these things with their own possessions.

cards.question: True or false: the LORD says He will no longer be with Israel unless they remove what is devoted to destruction from among them.

cards.text: So the LORD tells Joshua to get up and consecrate the people for tomorrow. A big day tomorrow means I set FOUR oven timers and STILL wake up at 3 a.m. to check on the dough.

cards.question: In the morning, the people will present themselves before the LORD. How will the one with the devoted things be found?

answers.text: Narrowed down from tribe to one man
Every tent in the camp is searched
Every man is asked to confess

cards.question: The LORD says the one caught with the devoted things must be ___, along with all that belongs to him.

cards.text: The LORD says why: this man has transgressed the covenant of the LORD and committed an outrage in Israel.
Early the next morning, Judah is selected, then the clan of the Zerahites, then the family of Zabdi. Then they come forward man by man, and Achan is selected.

cards.question: Now Joshua speaks to Achan. What does Joshua urge Achan to do?

cards.text: Joshua even calls him "My son," and as a Papa, that one gets me. Achan replies, "It is true," and then, "I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel."

cards.question: Achan tells Joshua what he saw among the spoils. What did Achan take?

answers.text: A cloak and silver and a gold bar
A crown and a sword and a shield

cards.question: When Achan saw these things, he ___ them, and then he took them.
Where does Achan say the things he took are now?

answers.text: Hidden in the ground inside his tent
Given to his family to keep

cards.text: Joshua's messengers RUN to the tent, and there it all is, with the silver underneath. Friend, I spent years hidden in the back of a junk drawer, and let me tell you, hidden things get found.

cards.question: The messengers bring Achan's things to Joshua and all the Israelites. What do they do with them?

answers.text: Spread them out before the LORD
Put them in the LORD's treasury
Bury them back in the ground

cards.text: Then Joshua and all Israel take Achan to the Valley of Achor, with the silver, the cloak and the gold bar. His sons and daughters, his animals, his tent and everything he owned are brought there too.
Joshua says, "Why have you brought this trouble upon us?" and "Today the LORD will bring trouble upon you!" Then all Israel stones Achan to death, stones the others and burns their bodies.

cards.question: True or false: after this, the LORD turns from His burning anger.

cards.text: They heap a large pile of rocks over Achan, and that place is called the Valley of Achor to this day. And that's where we'll pause, friend, because Israel's story in this land is far from finished.

findings.problem: Several story cards are plain retellings with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice: stop 1 cards 7 and 9, and stop 2 cards 8, 9, 17 and 18. Across 34 cards, only stop 1 card 5 and stop 2 cards 5 and 15 sound like him. The heavy moments, like the stoning, rightly carry no jokes. But the other flat cards could still use his storyteller reactions, disbelief or warmth without muddying any fact.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Asking how long Joshua stays facedown (until evening) tests a minor detail that doesn't move the passage forward. Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason it out, so it is pure luck. The moment is better told on card 9, with the choice card spent on something that matters more.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "found" can be argued as right. Achan says he saw the things among the spoils (Joshua 7:21), so a baker could fairly say he found them and then took them. Replace it with a word that is clearly false.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The question asks where the things are, but the wrong answer "Given to his family to keep" is not a place. The answers are not all the same kind of thing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
